item.title: Benchmarking Seven LLMs for Epilepsy MCQ Generation Reveals Strengths and Limits
item.description:
Benchmarking Seven LLMs for Epilepsy MCQ Generation Reveals Strengths and Limits

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate medical assessment items, but their reliability for disease‑specific question writing remains uncertain. A new benchmark evaluated seven publicly accessible LLMs on the task of creating single‑best‑answer epilepsy multiple‑choice questions (MCQs).

🔍 Overview

  • Purpose: Test how well current LLMs can draft epilepsy MCQs that meet educational standards.
  • Scope: Seven LLMs, 60 predefined tasks per model, total 420 generated questions.

⚙️ Benchmark Design

  • Prompt protocol: Identical single‑turn prompt for every model; no model‑specific tuning, web search, or external tools.
  • Task categories: Foundational knowledge, clinical cases, treatment decision‑making, diagnostic evaluation, longitudinal management.
  • Evaluation layers:
    • Objective metrics: structural compliance, keyed‑answer accuracy, textual characteristics, response time.
    • Expert review: Two blinded clinicians rated rigor, clarity, distractor quality, educational usefulness, cognitive alignment, and overall usability on five‑point scales.

📊 Results

  • Structural compliance: First‑pass compliance ranged from 83.33 % to 100 %; after one standardized corrective prompt, all 420 questions met structural requirements.
  • Keyed‑answer accuracy: Varied from 61.67 % to 98.33 %; Claude‑5 achieved the highest accuracy (98.33 %).
  • Composite expert scores (median):
    Model Composite Expert Score
    GPT‑5.6 3.75
    Claude‑5 3.67
    Kimi‑K3 3.50
  • Distractor quality: Median scores of only 2–3 across all models, indicating a common weakness.
  • Usability outcomes:
    • Directly usable without revision: 2 questions (0.48 %), both from GPT‑5.6.
    • Usable after minor revision: 119 questions (28.33 %).
    • Required substantial revision: 299 questions (71.19 %).
  • Additional observations:
    • Longer outputs correlated with better cognitive alignment but not with content rigor or clarity.
    • Response time showed no relationship to overall usability.

💡 Implications

  • Contemporary LLMs can reliably reproduce the structural format of epilepsy MCQs, yet structural compliance and answer accuracy alone do not guarantee educational readiness.
  • Weak distractor construction remains a major barrier to direct deployment.
  • LLMs may serve as assistants for expert‑supervised item drafting, but independent clinical review and subsequent learner‑based psychometric validation are still required before incorporation into medical education curricula.

#LLM #MedicalAI #EpilepsyEducation #MCQ

Source: Frontiers | Leveraging large language models to generate multiple-choice questions for epilepsy education

item.title: Pfizer‑Astellas Launches Independent Medical Education Grant for Bladder Cancer Care
item.description:
Pfizer‑Astellas Launches Independent Medical Education Grant for Bladder Cancer Care

The Pfizer–Astellas Independent Medical Education Grant supports U.S.‑based organizations that wish to develop educational projects on guideline‑concordant care for muscle‑invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and locally advanced or metastatic urothelial carcinoma (la/mUC).

📋 Eligibility

  • Projects must be conducted in the United States.
  • Applicant must be a U.S.‑based organization (individuals and independent practice groups are not eligible).
  • Eligible organizations include:
    • Medical, nursing, allied‑health, and pharmacy professional schools.
    • Healthcare institutions of any size.
  • The project/program lead must be an employee or contractor of the requesting organization and act as the applicant or authorized designee.
  • The requesting organization must be legally able to receive funding directly from Pfizer Inc.

💰 Funding Details

  • Funding range per project: $10,000 – $230,000
  • Maximum award: $230,000
  • Estimated total RFP budget: $900,000
  • Project duration: 18–24 months

📅 Timeline

Milestone Date
RFP release September 30, 2026
Application deadline November 10, 2026, 11:59 PM ET
Grant notification November 30, 2026
Project start (anticipated) February 2027
Project end (anticipated) July 2028

🖥️ Application Process

  • Submit applications through Pfizer’s MARCIE grant management system.
  • Complete all required sections of the online application.
  • Upload the full proposal in the designated Proposal/Protocol field.
  • For additional information on the Pfizer Competitive Grants Program and current oncology RFPs, visit the Pfizer Competitive Grants Program page.
  • To access the submission portal, use the Pfizer Grant Requester Portal.

🎯 Program Focus

  • Enable healthcare professionals to apply new and existing evidence for optimal MIBC and la/mUC care.
  • Emphasize guideline‑recommended first‑line treatment, peri‑operative therapies, adverse‑event management, multidisciplinary collaboration, and shared decision‑making.

#bladdercancer #medicaleducation #oncology #grant

Source: Pfizer–Astellas Independent Medical Education Grant: Up to $230,000 for MIBC and Advanced Urothelial Cancer - Oncology News, Insights, Stories by OncoDaily
